clue.text: Suspects something dodgy from note on lines in text by a traitor

indicators.note: in tells us the note and the lines are placed inside the word for a text message

parts.note: a text message is an SMS

indicators.note: on here means sitting before, so the note comes ahead of the lines

parts.note: E is a musical note
L is short for line, so LL is lines
a rat is someone who betrays their associates

explanation.surface: Someone reads a dubious passage by a turncoat and grows suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Text' looks like a passage of writing but is a phone message, and 'by a traitor' is a charade, not authorship.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is the idiom for sensing that something underhand is going on.

clue.text: Margin flanking a page

explanation.surface: A note on the edge of the paper beside the printed page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flanking' links the two senses: the strip at the side of a page, and one face of a sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is an edge or border region, and also one face of a leaf of paper, as in a two-sided essay.

clue.text: A collection of rhymed dactylics

indicators.note: of here says the answer is made of letters taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone describes an anthology of verse in a strict metre.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'rhymed' and the start of 'dactylics'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is a medieval Icelandic compilation of Norse mythological and heroic poems.

clue.text: A duke in Eilat twice ravaged a self-seeker's wife

indicators.note: ravaged suggests something torn apart, so these letters are thrown into a new order
twice says the town's name goes into the letter pool two times over

parts.note: Eilat, the Israeli resort town, taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman in an Israeli resort town wreaks havoc twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ravaged' scrambles A, D and EILATEILAT. Meredith's novel The Egoist has Sir Willoughby Patterne as its self-seeker; Laetitia Dale is the woman he finally marries.
explanation.definitionFit: In Meredith's The Egoist the self-absorbed Sir Willoughby ends up wedded to the patient Laetitia Dale.

clue.text: Introduce Latin at Cambridge University

parts.note: ad is a Latin preposition meaning to or at
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is a university in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: Someone brings classical language teaching into an English university.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cambridge meant is the one in Massachusetts, not the English university town.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to let them in or usher them into a place, a synonym of introduce.

clue.text: Herbert's spiritual work in a temporal revision

indicators.note: revision means reworking, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: George Herbert's religious verse is contrasted with a worldly rewrite of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' rearranges A TEMPORAL. George Herbert, the 17th-century religious poet, wrote 'The Altar', printed in the shape of an altar.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert's shaped poem 'The Altar' in The Temple is a devotional piece, hence a spiritual work.

clue.text: Returned expat Scottish author a lass finally met

parts.note: a gal is a girl or lass

indicators.note: finally picks only the closing letter of the word met

explanation.surface: A Scottish writer home from abroad, and the girl he eventually met.
explanation.walkthrough: John Galt, the Scottish novelist, spent years in Canada founding Guelph before coming back to Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: John Galt was a Scottish novelist who lived abroad in Canada and later went home, so a returned expatriate writer.

clue.text: Action by lady inspiring one prompting a person to make fair play judgements?

definitions.text: a person to make fair play judgements?

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the pair of words takes another piece inside it
by means next to, so the word for action stands beside the lady's name

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name, standing for a lady
do is an action or deed
a mover is one who prompts or sets things going

explanation.surface: A woman's deed spurs someone on to judge matters fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: Justice Adam Overdo is the magistrate in Ben Jonson's comedy Bartholomew Fair, who goes about the fair in disguise judging wrongdoing: hence a play about a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Justice Overdo is the magistrate in Jonson's Bartholomew Fair, judging the fairground's goings-on in disguise.

clue.text: Makes an appraisal of sums received by intellectual bookshop owner

definitions.text: sums received by intellectual bookshop owner

explanation.surface: A highbrow bookseller assesses the day's takings.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: takes (money received) and stock (a bookseller's goods) together describe a bookshop's business.
explanation.definitionFit: To take stock is the idiom for reviewing a situation before acting; takes are sums received, stock is a shop's goods.

clue.text: Author needing to perform with tool and worker in forge

parts.note: to do is to perform
a die is a tool for stamping or cutting shapes
a smith works metal at a forge

explanation.surface: A writer needs to act, plus a tool and a blacksmith.
explanation.walkthrough: Dodie Smith wrote I Capture the Castle and The Hundred and One Dalmatians.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodie Smith was an English novelist and playwright.

clue.text: A knave or a gentleman in a historic TV drama

definitions.text: a gentleman in a historic TV drama

explanation.surface: Is the man a rogue or a gentleman in a period television series?
explanation.walkthrough: In cards the knave is the jack; Gentleman Jack is a BBC period drama about Anne Lister.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack is the playing card also called the knave, and Gentleman Jack was the nickname of Anne Lister in the BBC series.

clue.text: Astrolabe production made this chap knackered once

definitions.text: Astrolabe production made this chap knackered once

parts.words: Astrolabe production made this chap knackered once
parts.note: Astrolabe was the son born to Héloïse and the medieval philosopher who was later castrated by her uncle's men, so the father of Astrolabe was once gelded

explanation.surface: Making a navigational instrument once wore out this fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Astrolabe looks like an instrument and like anagram fodder; it is the name of the son of Héloïse and the 12th-century philosopher. 'Knackered' is British slang for exhausted, but also literally gelded.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval French philosopher fathered a son named Astrolabe with Héloïse and was afterwards castrated.

clue.text: A kind of shark's seen on cold sea front in a tale of island life

parts.note: bitter weather is very cold
the lemon shark is a species of shark

indicators.note: front picks only the opening letter of the word sea

explanation.surface: A shark is spotted by a chilly shoreline in a story of island living.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence Durrell's Bitter Lemons recounts his years in Cyprus. The lemon shark is a real species.
explanation.definitionFit: Durrell's memoir of living in Cyprus is an account of life on an island.

clue.text: Hard gent involved with an organised crime ring

indicators.note: involved suggests something tangled, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A tough man is mixed up with a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges HARDGENT plus AN; 'with' only joins. The 'Ndrangheta is the Calabrian Mafia.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'Ndrangheta is a Calabrian mafia network, an organised criminal association.

clue.text: Fielding character dabbling with rude harlots and ribaldry initially? No Sir, rejected

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the five words it governs
rejected means turned back, so the two words are read from the end

explanation.surface: A Fielding figure flirts with lewd women and bawdiness, then is told 'No, sir!' and spurned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is skipped as a link. 'rejected' turns NOSIR into RISON. Dr Harrison is the upright clergyman in Fielding's Amelia, the ironic '?' since he does no such dabbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Harrison is the virtuous parson in Henry Fielding's novel Amelia.

clue.text: The acts of heroes in a celebration after some Bayreuth performances

indicators.note: after places the celebration behind the Wagner cycle

parts.note: Der Ring des Nibelungen, Wagner's opera cycle, is staged at Bayreuth over several evenings
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A party follows a run of Wagner operas at the festival.
explanation.walkthrough: DER RING is Wagner's Ring cycle, performed at the Bayreuth Festival over four nights.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is daring, heroic action of the sort found in adventure stories.

clue.text: One selling jewellery in Oliver!

explanation.surface: A jeweller appears in the musical about the orphan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oliver!' is the musical, but the Oliver meant is the Irish writer Oliver Goldsmith; 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A goldsmith makes and sells gold articles; Oliver Goldsmith wrote The Vicar of Wakefield.

clue.text: This is set up before court

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Something is erected ahead of a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect something is to build or raise it, the same as to put it up.

clue.text: Revolutionary trail followed by an Afro-Guyanese poet

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the whole pair is read backwards
followed by places the article after the trail

parts.note: a drag is a scent trail laid for hounds
an gives the article A

explanation.surface: A rebel trail leads to a Caribbean-born poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' turns DRAGA into AGARD. John Agard is a Guyanese-born poet living in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: John Agard is a poet born in British Guiana, of African heritage, long resident in Britain.

clue.text: Actor Herbert I see welcoming a famous playwright from northern Italy

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest in, so the playwright goes inside the other letters

parts.note: Herbert Lom was a film actor, famous in the Pink Panther films
I plus C, which sounds like see
the Bard is Shakespeare

explanation.surface: An actor makes Shakespeare welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: Herbert Lom was a Czech-born film actor, best known as Inspector Dreyfus in the Pink Panther films. Lombardy is the region round Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: Lombardic means relating to Lombardy, the region around Milan in northern Italy.

clue.text: No Oscar for English bandleader with musical routine in rep

indicators.note: no tells us a letter is taken away from the bandleader's name

parts.note: Geraldo was a popular English dance-band leader
Oscar is O in the radio alphabet
scales are practised as a routine by musicians

explanation.surface: An English band leader drops an award to play scales for a repertory company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes the final O from GERALDO. 'rep' looks like repertory theatre but means reprobate: Gerald Scales is the charming scoundrel in Arnold Bennett's The Old Wives' Tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Rep is short for reprobate, and Bennett's Gerald Scales is a rakish wastrel who deserts his wife.

clue.text: Disorder putting a horse right off, initially

parts.note: gee-gee is a childish word for a horse

indicators.note: initially picks only the first letter of the word off

explanation.surface: Someone causes trouble by putting a horse off.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive trouble or disturbance.

clue.text: The rounded character in a Noel Streatfeild novel, a Dane

definitions.text: in a Noel Streatfeild novel, a Dane

parts.note: the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A well-developed figure in a children's novel turns out to be Danish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounded character' looks like literary criticism but is the letter O. Theo Dane is the dancing teacher in Streatfeild's Ballet Shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ballet Shoes, the boarder Theo Dane teaches dancing, so her first name is that of the Dane.

clue.text: The god of interosculation?

indicators.note: of says the deity is made from letters inside the long word

explanation.surface: Which deity presides over kissing?
explanation.walkthrough: Interosculation means kissing, so the god of love fits the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love and desire.

clue.text: Fictional schoolboy from the orient, long before Hurree Jamset Ram Singh

explanation.surface: A storybook pupil from Asia, much earlier than the Greyfriars Indian prince.
explanation.walkthrough: East is Tom's friend in Tom Brown's Schooldays (1857), long before Hurree Jamset Ram Singh, the Indian boy of the Greyfriars school stories; 'from' and 'long before' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry East is Tom Brown's chum at Rugby, and the Orient means the countries of Asia.

clue.text: Someone putting all of her life into writing?

definitions.text: Someone putting all of her life into writing?

parts.words: Someone putting all of her life into writing?
parts.note: reads like a confessional author, but describes a writer recording another woman's whole life story

explanation.surface: A woman pours her whole life into her writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A life-writer records a subject's whole history, so the whole of her life goes onto the page.

clue.text: Girl's name in literary short stories

definitions.note: Girl's stands for girl is, a noun plus link

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for name inside the collection

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings about a writer

explanation.surface: A girl's name appears in a book of stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a common female first name.

clue.text: Trevor's work sold by 22 slyly

parts.note: refers to the answer of the clue numbered 22 down, a Streatfeild character's first name

indicators.note: slyly suggests craftiness, so the letters of the words are moved about

explanation.surface: A shop sells William Trevor's book through a cunning agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slyly' rearranges only the words 'sold by', which follow the cross-referenced name. The Old Boys is William Trevor's first acclaimed novel.
explanation.definitionFit: William Trevor's 1964 novel is about elderly former pupils of a public school.
